## Build CLI binding using Android NDK

### Prerequisites

- [Android NDK](https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides)
- [CMake](https://cmake.org/)

### Build

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git
cd llama.cpp

# Build the project
mkdir -p build-android
cd build-android
cmake -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$ANDROID_NDK_HOME/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake \
      -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a \
      -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-28 \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DGGML_RPC=ON \
      -DGGML_LLAMAFILE=ON \
      -DGGML_AVX=OFF \
      -DGGML_AVX2=OFF \
      -DGGML_AVX512=OFF \
      -DGGML_FMA=OFF \
      -DGGML_F16C=OFF \
      ..
cmake --build . --config Release -j $(nproc --all)

Based on the provided documentation, here is a structured summary and guide for using **llama.cpp** with **Ascend NPU** (CANN backend).

### 1. Overview
This backend integrates llama.cpp with Huawei's Ascend NPU using the CANN Toolkit. It supports both inference and training kernels via Ascend NPU directly.

### 2. System Requirements

#### Operating System
*   **Linux** (Verified on Ubuntu 22.04 and OpenEuler 22.03).

#### Hardware (Ascend NPU)
You can identify your device ID using:
```sh
lspci -n | grep -Eo '19e5:d[0-9a-f]{3}' | cut -d: -f2
```

### CUDA Graphs

llama.cpp supports CUDA graphs for faster inference. To enable this feature, use the `-ngl 100` command-line argument.

### CUDA Memory Pool

llama.cpp supports CUDA memory pool for faster inference. To enable this feature, use the `--cuda-mempool` command-line argument.

### CUDA Memory Alignment

llama.cpp supports CUDA memory alignment for faster inference. To enable this feature, use the `--cuda-mem-align` command-line argument.

### CUDA Memory Pool Alignment

llama.cpp supports CUDA memory pool alignment for faster inference. To enable this feature, use the `--cuda-mempool-align` command-line argument.

### CUDA Memory Pool Size

llama.cpp supports CUDA memory pool size for faster inference. To enable this feature, use the `--cuda-mempool-size` command-line argument.

To verify that the CPU is not oversaturated, you can use the `htop` command to monitor CPU usage. If you see that the CPU is at 100% usage, then you should reduce the number of threads.

## Verifying that the GPU is not oversaturated
llama accepts a `-ngl N` (or `--n-gpu-layers N`) flag to configure the number of layers to offload to the GPU. If you set this to a very large number, then the GPU will be oversaturated, and the CPU will be starved of data. This will result in poor performance.

To verify that the GPU is not oversaturated, you can use the `nvidia-smi` command to monitor GPU usage. If you see that the GPU is at 100% usage, then you should reduce the number of layers.
